full_judgment:
Muhammad Abdur Rouf J:- This appeal on leave by the defendants is from the judgment and order dated June 18, 1992 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Case No. 7614 of 1991 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated July 31, 1991 passed by the Subordinate judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 112 of 1990 reversing the judgment and decree dated February 28, 1990 passed by the Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka dismissing Title Suit No. 818 of 1987. 

 4. The trial Court in dismissing the suit held that the plaintiff had illegally occupied the University Quarter in question and violated the instruction given by the concerned authority for vacating the quarter and that upon giving by the concerned authority for vacating the quarter and that upon giving him all possible opportunities he was legally removed from service. The Lower appellate Court, however, reversed the decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit holding that for unauthorized occupation the standard rent could be charged against him under the Accommodation Rules of the University. His removal from service on the ground of such unauthorised occupation was not warranted by any law. Moreover, the concerned authority did not follow the procedure provided in Article 38(4) of the Dhaka University Order, 1973, (there is no relevancy of the mentioned article which is presumed to be wrongly mentioned in place of mentioning Statute 45(4) of the First Statutes of the Dhaka University) regarding constitution of a tribunal for holding inquiry against the respondent and that subsequent addition of the ground of 'misconduct' by a belated amendment on 18-2-86 in the removal order had been done in violation of the principle of natural justice. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment held that sub-article (4) of Article 45, (wrongly mentioned as an "article" which should have been mentioned as clause 4 of Statute 45 of the First Statutes of the University because "article" is used in P.O. No. 11 of 1973 as the article of that Order), although applicable to the plaintiff was not complied with in removing him from service. The order of dismissal was illegal being made without jurisdiction and in violation of the principle of natural justice. 

 6. Mr. Md. Abdur Rashid, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand supported the findings of the lower appellate Court and the High Court Division. He further submitted that the impugned order having been passed without complying with the principle of natural justice, the lower appellate Court and the High Court Division rightly decreed the suit. 

 13. The appeal is allowed without cost. The judgment and order appealed against and also the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, on 31-7-91 in Title Appeal No. 112 of 1990 are set aside and the judgment and decree of the teamed Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka passed on 28-2-90 in Tide Suit. No. 818 of 1987, dismissing the suit, is restored.
